title: Disjointness of support fibers over distinct sets
statement: Fix a word $u$ of length $n$ over a finite alphabet, and let $S$ and $T$ be two distinct sets of coordinate positions in $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$. Then the support fiber of $u$ over $S$ and the support fiber of $u$ over $T$ are disjoint: no word $v$ can differ from $u$ at exactly the positions in $S$ while also differing from $u$ at exactly the positions in $T$.
hypotheses_covered: u is a word of length n over a finite alphabet
S and T are sets of coordinate positions
replaced:
If $S \ne T$ are distinct finsets of coordinate positions, then
$\mathrm{supportFiber}(u,S)$ and $\mathrm{supportFiber}(u,T)$ are disjoint finsets.
